_note: Decision 6.2 in code, Module 4 of the founder's Control Tower & GilbertOne Commercialization plan (proposed 23 September 2026): 'The knowledge corpus is split... Retrieval is clinical behaviour below the emergency backstop.' Phase 0, contract-authoring only. Checked against the tree on 24 September 2026 rather than assumed: apps/assistant-api/src/lib/knowledge.ts builds one undivided in-memory index over all 261 entries under packages/catalog/knowledge, and scripts/ingest-knowledge-embeddings.mjs embeds and upserts that same undivided set of 261 entries into one Qdrant collection, on every run, with no distinction of any kind between an entry that states a clinical fact and an entry that names a helpline. Both are wired live: apps/assistant-api/src/lib/tools/knowledge-search.ts calls retrieveKnowledge() as a tool the model tier may invoke, gated only by whatever gates the LLM tier as a whole (a configured provider, MYTHUSO_ASSISTANT_PRODUCTION=acknowledged) — dark today, but the corpus behind it, once that gate opens, is one corpus, not two. This file proposes the split and specifies where it would go in; it does not build it, and scripts/ingest-knowledge-embeddings.mjs is unchanged by this file.
_source: Decision 6.2, verbatim: 'The knowledge corpus is split. Clinical corpus — locked. Refreshed only through the Clinician Review Queue, versioned, rolled back through the same path. Non-clinical corpus — self-improving. Refreshed autonomously through scripts/ingest-knowledge-embeddings.mjs. The build fails if the clinical corpus is refreshed outside the Review Queue path.'
_tensionWithTheScopeDocument: docs/COMMERCIAL-AND-CONTROL-TOWER-SCOPE.md section 2's self-learning table (written the day before this module) lists 'Retrieval quality (knowledge-embedding refresh)' as an unqualified 'Yes — MAY self-improve... via the existing scripts/ingest-knowledge-embeddings.mjs', and lists 'Non-clinical knowledge... service navigation, directory, programme info' as a second, narrower 'Yes' beside it. Read together, that table already contains the seam decision 6.2 asks to be made explicit: the broad 'retrieval refresh may self-improve' license was never meant to cover the clinical half of what that same script actually refreshes, only the narrower non-clinical one sitting beside it in the same table. This file is that correction, made precise rather than left as two adjacent table rows a reader could reconcile either way.

corpusToday.keywordIndex: apps/assistant-api/src/lib/knowledge.ts builds one in-memory TF-IDF-style index (CORPUS) over all 261 entries at module load, searched by searchKnowledge() and cached in one process-wide LRU (cache, 200 entries) with no tier or tenant segment of any kind in its key.
corpusToday.vectorIndex: scripts/ingest-knowledge-embeddings.mjs calls knowledgeChunks() — which returns exactly the same 261 entries the keyword index reads — and embeds and upserts every one of them into one Qdrant collection (QDRANT_COLLECTION, default "gilbertone-knowledge"), unconditionally, on every run. Nothing in the script reads, checks or even carries any field that could distinguish a clinical entry from a non-clinical one; KnowledgeChunk's own shape (id, title, source, file, snippet, text) drops the entry's evidenceGrade before it ever reaches the script.
corpusToday.liveWiring: apps/assistant-api/src/lib/tools/knowledge-search.ts imports retrieveKnowledge() and exposes it as a tool the orchestrator's model tier may call. This is not dark by contract the way knowledge-federation.ts's external sources are (every one ships active: false, and only the founder's demonstration override of 2 October 2026 opens any of them, through the reference_sources tool) — the local corpus itself is reachable the day the LLM tier's own gates (a configured Azure provider, MYTHUSO_ASSISTANT_PRODUCTION=acknowledged) open, with no further switch of its own.

theSeamAlreadyInTheData.field: Every knowledge entry's source.evidenceGrade, defined once in packages/catalog/knowledge/federation.json's evidenceGrades block: "guideline" (clinical or public-health guidance from a named authority), "regulatory-label" (a regulator's product-label wording paired with SA treatment-guideline counterpart — interactions.json only), and "not-assessed" ("service navigation, programme or directory information carried for completeness — no clinical evidence assessment has been performed on the entry, and none is implied").
theSeamAlreadyInTheData.whyThisFieldAndNotAFileList: evidenceGrade is entry-level, not file-level, and the difference is not cosmetic: maternal.json carries 19 guideline entries and one not-assessed entry (mat-016, 'MomConnect — Free Pregnancy Messages', an SMS-registration service, not a clinical fact); mental-health.json carries 13 guideline entries and one not-assessed entry (mh-014, 'South African Crisis and Support Lines Directory', a phone-number directory). A file-level rule — 'maternal.json is clinical, sa-health-system.json is not' — would either lock two harmless directory entries behind a review queue for no safety reason, or leave them unlocked by exempting the whole file they happen to sit in. Tiering by evidenceGrade instead of by file gets both entries right without a special case, because the catalog's own maintainers already recorded, entry by entry, which of these carry a clinical evidence assessment and which do not.
theSeamAlreadyInTheData.whatThisFileProposes: Clinical corpus = every entry whose source.evidenceGrade is "guideline" or "regulatory-label" (245 of 261, spanning all nine files to varying degrees). Non-clinical corpus = every entry whose source.evidenceGrade is "not-assessed" (16 of 261: all 14 of sa-health-system.json, plus mat-016 and mh-014).

corpusTiers.label: Clinical corpus
corpusTiers.sentence: Locked. No entry is added, edited or re-embedded except through a ratified entry in packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json naming exactly that change. Versioned and rolled back through the same path, the same discipline that queue already states for escalation.ts and gilbert-emergency-terms.json in packages/catalog/gilbert-clinical-core.json.
corpusTiers.why: A condition's symptom list, a medicine's dosage, a recorded drug interaction — every one of these is content a nurse or doctor could act on without re-deriving it themselves if GilbertOne surfaces it in an answer, which is this module's own framing of why retrieval is a clinical act rather than a librarian's task.

corpusTiers.label: Non-clinical corpus
corpusTiers.sentence: Self-improving. Refreshed autonomously through scripts/ingest-knowledge-embeddings.mjs, on any schedule, with no queue entry required.
corpusTiers.why: A MomConnect registration code and a crisis-line phone number are navigational facts, not clinical ones — the same category docs/COMMERCIAL-AND-CONTROL-TOWER-SCOPE.md's self-learning table already names as free to self-improve ('service navigation, directory, programme info'), and locking them behind a clinical review queue would spend that mechanism's authority on content that carries no clinical risk to begin with.

refreshRouting._note: What scripts/ingest-knowledge-embeddings.mjs and knowledge.ts's KnowledgeChunk/knowledgeChunks() would need to carry for the split above to be enforceable. Described, not built — this file changes neither.
gaps: KnowledgeChunk (knowledge.ts) does not carry source.evidenceGrade today; only the attribution string (source) survives into the chunk a script or a Qdrant payload ever sees. Nothing downstream of knowledgeChunks() can currently tell a clinical entry from a non-clinical one, even by accident, because the field that would let it is dropped before that point.

ingest-knowledge-embeddings.mjs calls knowledgeChunks() once and embeds/upserts the entire return value into one collection in one run. There is no tier-aware branch anywhere in the script — no filter, no second collection, no flag.
wouldNeed: knowledgeChunks() (or a wrapper the script reads instead) to carry each entry's evidenceGrade or a tier derived from it through to the embeddable record, so a refresh path can select on it.

Either two Qdrant collections (one per tier — structurally the stronger isolation, because an unfiltered non-clinical-refresh run becomes physically unable to touch the clinical collection) or one collection with a tier field in every point's payload plus a mandatory filter the refresh path applies without exception (weaker, because it depends on the refresh script remembering to filter, the same distinction packages/catalog/gilbertone-inference-isolation.json draws between separate embedding partitions and a filtered shared one).
A non-clinical-only refresh entry point, runnable unattended on any schedule, touching only entries where evidenceGrade is not-assessed.

A clinical refresh entry point that refuses to run — non-zero exit, a message naming what is missing, the same discipline the script already applies to a missing Azure credential — unless invoked with a reference to a ratified packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json entry naming exactly the knowledge-catalog file or entry ids it is about to re-embed. This mirrors packages/catalog/gilbert-clinical-core.json's no-auto-promotion-without-a-signature refusal, applied to a corpus refresh instead of an escalation-rule change.

queueFitFlag.doesNotYetFit: packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json's tiers array (1 — global core, 2 — per-tenant additive, device) has no shape for what a clinical-corpus refresh actually is: a bulk re-embedding of up to 245 already-existing catalog entries, not one atomic change. That queue's own entryShape.proposedChangeRef is built to name one thing — a protocol id, a device-threshold rule id, or one diff to escalation.ts — never a batch of many existing entries being re-embedded together, and never a single new or edited knowledge entry either, since knowledge.json entries currently have no queue concept applied to them at all (unlike protocols.json's own draft/ratified states).
twoWaysItCouldFit: A fourth tier id (for example "clinical-corpus"), scoped globally like Tier 1 rather than per-tenant, whose proposedChangeRef can name a knowledge-catalog file plus an entry-id list or a git commit range, rather than the single id every existing tier's entries name today.

Treat each clinical-tier knowledge entry's addition or edit as an ordinary Tier-1-shaped queue entry, filed one at a time — accepting that a multi-entry catalog update becomes several queue entries rather than one, with no schema change to the queue itself.
queueFitFlag.notDecidedHere: This file does not choose between the two, and does not edit packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json to add either shape — that file was authored by a sibling module today and a schema change to it is that module's call, not this one's. This is named as an open item for whoever owns that file, per this task's own instruction not to silently assume a fit that has not been checked.

refusals.statement: No entry whose source.evidenceGrade is guideline or regulatory-label is added to, edited in, or re-embedded into the corpus a person's question is answered from, except through a ratified entry in packages/catalog/clinical-review-queue.json naming exactly that change. Today, neither the queue nor the merge path this would need exists, and scripts/ingest-knowledge-embeddings.mjs re-embeds all 245 clinical-tier entries on every run with no gate of any kind — so this rule is already unenforced by the tree as it stands, not merely unbuilt for a future case.
refusals.why: Retrieval is clinical behaviour below the emergency backstop: a nurse or doctor reading a retrieved snippet is reading something GilbertOne chose to put in front of them, which is exactly the kind of change gilbert-clinical-core.json already treats as requiring a signature, restated here for what is retrievable rather than for a rule that fires.

refusals.statement: An entry whose source.evidenceGrade is not-assessed may be added, edited and re-embedded by scripts/ingest-knowledge-embeddings.mjs running autonomously, on any schedule, with no queue entry.
refusals.why: docs/COMMERCIAL-AND-CONTROL-TOWER-SCOPE.md's own self-learning table already names service navigation, directory and programme information as free to self-improve. Locking a MomConnect registration code or a crisis-line phone number behind the same review queue that guards a drug interaction would spend the queue's authority — and a clinician reviewer's time — on content that carries no clinical risk, which is the surest way to make the queue feel like paperwork rather than a safety gate.

refusals.statement: A knowledge entry's tier is read from its own source.evidenceGrade field, never inferred from which catalog file it lives in, its title, or a keyword match against its content.
refusals.why: maternal.json and mental-health.json each already carry one not-assessed entry alongside their otherwise-clinical content. A file-level or keyword-based rule would misclassify both — either locking harmless directory content behind clinical review, or leaving it unlocked by exempting the whole file it happens to sit in.

refusals.statement: This file proposes reusing evidenceGrade — recorded on 21 September 2026 for editorial attribution, not for a refresh-gating purpose — as the boundary decision 6.2 asks for. That reuse has not itself been reviewed by whoever ratifies clinical governance decisions, and nothing before that review may treat the boundary as clinically authoritative.
refusals.why: The same distinction packages/catalog/gilbert-clinical-core.json draws for its own locked artifacts: naming something as the mechanism a rule will use fixes what the rule points at, it does not upgrade that thing's own standing. Conflating 'this field is a convenient existing seam' with 'this field has been clinically validated as the correct clinical/non-clinical boundary' would be exactly the overstatement CLAUDE.md's rule against a health service overstating its readiness exists to catch.

refusals.statement: Nothing may claim the clinical/non-clinical corpus split described here is enforced until knowledgeChunks() carries evidenceGrade through to the embeddable record and scripts/ingest-knowledge-embeddings.mjs reads it — both unchanged by this file. Until then, every run of that script refreshes all 261 entries as one corpus, exactly as it does today.
refusals.why: Naming a split in a contract does not build it. A build or a deploy note that cited this file as though the corpus were already partitioned would be describing a script this file explicitly says it has not touched.

preview: No entry has ever been withheld from a refresh, no collection has ever been split, and knowledgeChunks() has never carried an evidence grade past its own module. This file names the seam (source.evidenceGrade) the split would use, the sixteen entries it would place in the non-clinical corpus today, and what scripts/ingest-knowledge-embeddings.mjs and the Clinician Review Queue would each need before either sentence in decision 6.2 became true of the running system.
